
7s Block Double-Zeta Basis Set Archive
=====================================


Date: 27 Mar 2007


When publishing work that uses these basis sets, please use the following citation:

K.G. Dyall, in preparation. Available from the Dirac web site, http://dirac.chem.sdu.dk.



This archive contains the exponents and the SCF orbital coefficients, given with
respect to normalized (spherical or 2-spinor) Gaussian functions, for the basis
sets described in the above article. The SCF exponent sets reported include the
functions for the 7p, the correlating d function for the 6s and 6p shells, and
the correlating f function for the 5d shell. The d and f sets were reoptimized
after addition or replacement of the correlating function, which was held fixed.
In all the following descriptions, this is the set referred to as the SCF
exponent set.

The archive is set out as follows.

1. Exponents and SCF coefficients for Dirac-Hartree-Fock wave functions, in order
   of Z. The large component functions are given first, followed by the small 
   component functions. Both components are labelled with the large component
   symmetry type, but the primitive functions for the small component are
   those obtained by restricted kinetic balance from the large component.
   The spin-orbit components have a "-" label for j=l-1/2 and a "+" label for
   j=l+1/2.

2. Exponents and SCF coefficients for spin-free modified Dirac-Hartree-Fock wave
   functions, in order of Z. The large component functions are given first, 
   followed by the pseudo-large component functions, then the Foldy-Wouthuysen
   transformed large component functions. Note that all components have the same
   symmetry type. 

3. Exponents of correlating functions, valence (d) and core (f).

4. Exponents of 6s6p dipole polarization functions


Basis set construction.
----------------------

For the s elements, the outer core (n-1)s and (n-1)p must be included in the valence.
For Ra, the valence np is considered an occupied orbital and is correlated; hence 
there is an extra correlating d function for Ra. 

Several different types of basis sets may be constructed by adding primitive 
functions to the SCF set. These basis sets are described below.

NOTE: Functions are counted from the function with the smallest exponent to the largest. 

1. Valence and outer core. To the SCF occupied set, add the following:
   1st and 3rd s primitives from the SCF set
   1st and 3rd p primitives from the SCF set
   1st d primitive from the SCF set (correlating d for 6p) 
   Valence correlating d function for Ra

   (HF + 2s2p1d/2d valence/outer core)


2. 5d correlation. To basis set 1, add the following:
   5th s primitive from the SCF set
   5th p primitive from the SCF set
   3rd d primitive from the SCF set
   1st f primitive from the SCF set (correlating f).

   (HF + 2s2p1d/2d valence/outer core + 1s1p1d1f core)


3. Outer core (6s6p) dipole polarization. To any of the above basis sets, add the 
   s, p, and d polarizing functions.





Dirac-Hartree-Fock basis sets           
=============================           




** Fr **
